summary: Dan Li works in linguistics and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sherab Gyatso and served as an associate professor at Soka University (attested 2026).

Dan Lusthaus specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at Temple University under several scholars, taught at institutions including Grinnell, Georgia, UCLA, and Florida State, and was a research associate at Harvard in 2005.

Dan Martin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Indiana University Bloomington (~1983–1991), studying under Elliot Sperling, and held posts at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, Carnegie Mellon, and Hebrew University.

Dan Smyer Yü works in religious studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of California, Davis, and served as a research group leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who earned his Ph.D. at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and his Dr.phil. at the University of Copenhagen. He has served as professor and Center for Subjectivity Research director at Copenhagen and as professor at Oxford.

Daniel Aaron Getz specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, also studying under Ying-shih Yü and Tairyō Makita, and held a post as associate professor at Bradley University (attested 2019).
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He held assistant professorships at Butler University (attested 1986) and the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003), and was a guest scholar at Soka University.
Daniel Borengasser works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned his Master of Arts at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley.

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Indology. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington and earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair. He has served as an associate professor at Cornell University.
Daniel Clarke Waugh works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and archaeology. He earned degrees from Yale and Harvard before joining the faculty at the University of Washington in 1972.

Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Harvard, Berlin, and Cambridge. He served as librarian at Yale, president of the University of California, founding president of Johns Hopkins University, and president of both the American Oriental Society and the Carnegie Institution.

Daniel Cozort specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, studied under several traditional teachers, and held academic positions at Bates College and Dickinson College.

Daniel Dubuisson works in religious studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. Around 1993, he served as a director of research at CNRS and the University of Lille, and held a post at University Lille-III.

Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indologist and philosopher. Educated at Harvard and in India under Kalipada Tarkacharya and Walter Eugene Clark, he was a Junior Fellow and served as Wales Professor of Sanskrit at Harvard University.

Daniel John Gogerly worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He led the Wesleyan Mission Press (~1818–1822), chaired the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society in 1838, and served as secretary, vice-president, and president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka.

Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn. He was a longtime professor at the University of British Columbia (~1973–2001).

Daniel M. Neuman specializes in Indology and ethnomusicology. He studied at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Chicago, holding academic posts at Dartmouth College, the University of Washington, and UCLA.

Daniel M. Stuart specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He received his Ph.D. from UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt and held appointments at the University of South Carolina (attested 2017) and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Daniel M. Veidlinger works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, served as a research associate at Chiang Mai University in 1999, and held a post at California State University, Chico.
